meta.title: The Golden Bracelet
meta.textType: story: two versions of one event

paragraphs: On Saturday, the family had a picnic in the nature park, and Pip found a golden bracelet. That evening, Lily wrote about it in her diary. On Monday, Tom told the same story to Ben at lunch. The two stories were not exactly the same.

Lily's diary, Saturday night. Today we sat at a table in the picnic area near the pond. Pip ran to a bench and made a loud noise at something under it. I looked under the bench and saw a golden bracelet. "I think it belongs to a schoolchild," I said. There was a small name on it, but I could not read it. "Whose bracelet is it?" I asked Dad. "I do not know, but a child will look for it," said Dad. "Let's give it to Ranger Mark," I said. Ranger Mark was very helpful, and he put the bracelet in a small box.

After ten minutes, a girl in a yellow T-shirt ran to the office of Ranger Mark. "That is my bracelet!" she said. Ranger Mark returned it to her, and she said thank you three times. We ate ice cream to celebrate, and Pip got a little piece of bread. It was a very good day.

Tom's story on Monday, at lunch. "On Saturday, we ate our picnic by the pond," said Tom. "Pip ran into the tall grass near the path and made a lot of noise." "I went after him and found a golden bracelet on the ground." "This belongs to a schoolchild," I said, and I showed it to Mom. "Take it to Ranger Mark," Mom told me. "Ranger Mark certainly knew what to do."

"The girl came after twenty minutes," said Tom. "Her mom came with her, and she held the bracelet very hard." "Then Dad bought a cold drink for everybody." "We celebrated, and Pip slept under the table." Ben listened with big eyes. "Was the girl happy?" he asked. "Very happy," said Tom. Then Ben said, "This morning, Lily told me about the ice cream and the bench." "Then ask her again, because I am sure about the cold drink," said Tom with a smile.
Ben laughed. "You both tell a good story," he said. "I am happy that the girl got her bracelet again." "That is the same in both stories," said Tom.

sentences.text: On Saturday, the family had a picnic in the nature park, and Pip found a golden bracelet.
That evening, Lily wrote about it in her diary.
On Monday, Tom told the same story to Ben at lunch.
The two stories were not exactly the same.
Lily's diary, Saturday night.
Today we sat at a table in the picnic area near the pond.
Pip ran to a bench and made a loud noise at something under it.
I looked under the bench and saw a golden bracelet.
"I think it belongs to a schoolchild," I said.
There was a small name on it, but I could not read it.
"Whose bracelet is it?" I asked Dad.
"I do not know, but a child will look for it," said Dad.
"Let's give it to Ranger Mark," I said.
Ranger Mark was very helpful, and he put the bracelet in a small box.
After ten minutes, a girl in a yellow T-shirt ran to the office of Ranger Mark.
"That is my bracelet!" she said.
Ranger Mark returned it to her, and she said thank you three times.
We ate ice cream to celebrate, and Pip got a little piece of bread.
It was a very good day.
Tom's story on Monday, at lunch.
"On Saturday, we ate our picnic by the pond," said Tom.
"Pip ran into the tall grass near the path and made a lot of noise."
"I went after him and found a golden bracelet on the ground."
"This belongs to a schoolchild," I said, and I showed it to Mom.
"Take it to Ranger Mark," Mom told me.
"Ranger Mark certainly knew what to do."
"The girl came after twenty minutes," said Tom.
"Her mom came with her, and she held the bracelet very hard."
"Then Dad bought a cold drink for everybody."
"We celebrated, and Pip slept under the table."
Ben listened with big eyes.
"Was the girl happy?" he asked.
"Very happy," said Tom.
Then Ben said, "This morning, Lily told me about the ice cream and the bench."
"Then ask her again, because I am sure about the cold drink," said Tom with a smile.
Ben laughed.
"You both tell a good story," he said.
"I am happy that the girl got her bracelet again."
"That is the same in both stories," said Tom.
